name: Vote for Me!

pick.label: Pick a cause
pick.heading: Pick a cause and start a party
lead: German ballot papers can be very long. There is a party for animal welfare, and even one that exists mainly to make fun of all the others.
Choose a cause from the shelf, or bring your own, and build a whole party around it. *Nobody asked for it. That has never stopped anyone.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Obviously I am not looking for a serious manifesto here, this is just for a bit of fun. Some of these parties would win a landslide in Friedrichshain and lose everywhere else. That’s fine.

shelf.head: In your city
items: A tram to the Baltic Sea
A public sauna in every Kiez

shelf.head: On campus
items: A nap room in every building

shelf.head: Everyday life
items: Free repairs for anything with a plug
A day off on your birthday
A four-day weekend once a month

shelf.head: Big ideas
items: Free pizza at every polling station

rows: Which promise from the shelf (or your own) is your party built on?
Something people will remember on the ballot paper. Bonus points for a good abbreviation.
What exactly will you do, and how fast? Be specific: politicians never are.
Who votes for you first? Students, night owls, dog owners, people who are just very tired?
Short enough for a poster on a lamp post.
How do you get people talking about you? A stunt, a celebrity, a song, a TV debate?

values.promise: Every Kiez gets a proper bakery within five minutes’ walk, open all day on Sundays, and the state pays for the ovens. On my first day I appoint a Minister for Breakfast.
values.voters: Everyone who has ever stood outside a closed bakery on a Sunday morning, slightly hungover, holding a two-euro coin and no plan B.
values.campaign: Handing out free warm Schrippen at every U-Bahn station on the Sunday before the election. My opponents will call it bribery. It is, but it’s delicious bribery.

yours.label: Your party
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your party in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which party wins the election?
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their party in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
